description: Master agile backlog. All epics, features, stories, and requirements from this epic forward.

epic.name: Evaluate Care v0.1.4

feature.name: Provider Quality Scoring Engine
feature.description: Deterministic composite scoring engine that aggregates multiple provider quality measures into a single score with fixed weighting logic.

story.description: Create Pydantic models for provider quality score input (measures, weights, metadata) and output (composite score, subscores, trace). Ensure compatibility with existing provider_detail_service data structures.

requirement.requirement: The system must define a Pydantic input model that accepts a list of provider quality measures with name, value, and optional metadata fields.
requirement.name: Define Pydantic model for provider quality measures list with optional metadata

requirement.requirement: The system must define a Pydantic input model that includes a weights structure mapping each measure to a numeric weight.
requirement.name: Pydantic input model with weights mapping measures to numeric values

requirement.requirement: The system must enforce via schema validation that all weights are numeric and non-negative.
requirement.name: Enforce schema: all weights must be numeric and non-negative

requirement.requirement: The system must enforce via schema validation that each measure in the input has a corresponding weight entry.
requirement.name: Schema validation requires weight entry for each input measure

requirement.requirement: The system must define a Pydantic output model containing a composite_score field as a numeric value.
requirement.name: Define Pydantic output model with numeric composite_score field

requirement.requirement: The system must define a Pydantic output model containing subscores for each measure used in scoring.
requirement.name: Define Pydantic output model with subscores for each scoring measure

requirement.requirement: The system must define a Pydantic output model containing a trace field that captures measure inputs, weights, and intermediate values used in score calculation.
requirement.name: Pydantic output model with trace field for inputs, weights, intermediates

requirement.requirement: The system must ensure the schema supports serialization to JSON without loss of numeric precision for scores and weights.
requirement.name: Schema must support JSON serialization preserving numeric precision for scores/​

requirement.requirement: The system must ensure compatibility of the input schema with provider data structures returned by provider_detail_service without requiring transformation outside the schema layer.
requirement.name: Ensure input schema matches provider_detail_service data, no external transforms

requirement.requirement: The system must validate that measure values conform to expected numeric types or explicitly defined categorical encodings.
requirement.name: Validate measure values as correct numeric types or defined categorical encoders

requirement.requirement: The system must raise a validation error when required fields (measures or weights) are missing from the input payload.
requirement.name: Raise validation error if measures or weights fields are missing from input

requirement.requirement: The system must raise a validation error when a measure value is null or undefined for required measures.
requirement.name: Raise validation error if required measure value is null or undefined

requirement.requirement: The system must allow optional metadata fields in the input schema without failing validation when additional fields are present.
requirement.name: Allow optional metadata fields in input without validation failure for extras

requirement.requirement: The system must ensure deterministic field naming and structure in both input and output schemas across all invocations.
requirement.name: Ensure deterministic field naming and structure in all schemas

requirement.requirement: The system must support extensibility in the schema such that new measures can be added without breaking backward compatibility of existing fields.
requirement.name: Support schema extensibility for new measures with backward compatibility

story.name: Define provider score schema and contract

story.description: Build backend service that computes composite provider score using fixed weighting logic, normalization, and aggregation across measures. No randomness; same input must always yield same output.

requirement.requirement: The system must preserve numerical precision to at least two decimal places in all score outputs.
requirement.name: Preserve at least two decimal places precision in all score outputs

requirement.requirement: The system must handle missing measure values by excluding them from aggregation while preserving remaining weights proportionally.
requirement.name: Exclude missing measures from aggregation; adjust remaining weights proportionly

requirement.requirement: The system must return a valid composite score when at least one valid measure is present in the input.
requirement.name: Return composite score if input includes at least one valid measure

requirement.requirement: The system must compute a composite provider score using only deterministic functions with no randomness or time-based inputs.
requirement.name: Compute provider score using deterministic, non-random, non-temporal functions

requirement.requirement: The system must produce identical composite scores when given identical input payloads across repeated executions.
requirement.name: Consistent composite scores for identical input payloads across executions

requirement.requirement: The system must normalize all input measures to a consistent scale before aggregation.
requirement.name: Normalize all input measures to a consistent scale before aggregation

requirement.requirement: The system must apply fixed weighting logic as defined in the input schema without modifying weights at runtime.
requirement.name: Apply fixed weighting from schema without runtime modification

requirement.requirement: The system must compute the composite score as a weighted aggregation of all normalized measures.
requirement.name: Compute composite score as weighted aggregation of normalized measures

requirement.requirement: The system must return both the composite score and individual measure contributions in the output structure.
requirement.name: Return composite score and individual measure contributions in output

requirement.requirement: The system must raise a deterministic error response when all measures are missing or invalid.
requirement.name: Deterministic error if all measures are missing or invalid

requirement.requirement: The system must validate that the sum of weights is greater than zero before performing aggregation.
requirement.name: Validate sum of weights > 0 before aggregation

requirement.requirement: The system must raise a deterministic error response when the sum of weights equals zero.
requirement.name: Raise deterministic error if sum of weights equals zero

requirement.requirement: The system must not mutate the input payload during score computation.
requirement.name: Prevent input payload mutation during score computation

requirement.requirement: The system must execute scoring logic within a bounded time threshold suitable for synchronous API usage.
requirement.name: Scoring logic executes within synchronous API time threshold

story.name: Implement deterministic scoring engine core logic

story.description: Expose provider scoring through evaluate_care_facade, wiring score computation into existing provider evaluation flow and returning score payload to callers.

requirement.requirement: The system must not introduce randomness or non-deterministic behavior in score computation or response formatting.
requirement.name: No randomness or non-determinism in scores or response formatting

requirement.requirement: The system must integrate scoring without increasing evaluate_care_facade response latency beyond acceptable service thresholds.
requirement.name: Integrate scoring with evaluate_care_facade latency within service thresholds

requirement.name: Return provider details even if scoring is disabled or not requested

requirement.requirement: The system must return a composite provider score in the evaluate_care_facade response payload.
requirement.name: Return composite provider score in evaluate_care_facade response payload

requirement.requirement: The system must include measure-level subscores in the response payload when available from the scoring engine.
requirement.name: Include measure-level subscores in response payload when available

requirement.requirement: The system must include scoring trace metadata (weights and inputs used) in the response payload.
requirement.name: Include scoring trace metadata (weights and inputs) in response payload

requirement.requirement: The system must ensure that identical provider inputs produce identical score outputs through the facade.
requirement.name: Ensure identical provider inputs yield identical scores via the facade

requirement.requirement: The system must gracefully handle missing provider measure data by returning a partial score or null score with an explanatory flag.
requirement.name: Handle missing provider data with partial/null score and explanatory flag

requirement.requirement: The system must return an error indicator in the response if the scoring engine fails during execution.
requirement.name: Return error indicator if scoring engine fails during execution

requirement.requirement: The system must log scoring engine invocation and outputs for observability within the evaluate_care_facade flow.
requirement.name: Log scoring engine invocation and outputs in evaluate_care_facade flow

requirement.requirement: The system must ensure the scoring payload structure conforms to the schema defined in EVAL-SP-001.
requirement.name: Enforce scoring payload structure per EVAL-SP-001 schema

requirement.requirement: The system must not break existing evaluate_care_facade response fields when adding scoring output.
requirement.name: Preserve evaluate_care_facade response fields when adding scoring output

requirement.requirement: The system must allow downstream LLM consumers to access composite score, subscores, and trace fields in a single response object.
requirement.name: Expose composite score, subscores, and trace in one response object

requirement.requirement: The system must structure the scoring output in a way that enables LLMs to generate explanations without additional transformations.
requirement.name: Structure scoring output to support LLM explanation generation without reformat

requirement.requirement: The system must include explicit null or fallback values for any missing scoring components to prevent LLM hallucination.
requirement.name: Use explicit null or fallback values for missing scoring components

requirement.requirement: The system must ensure all numeric score fields are normalized to a consistent scale for LLM interpretability.
requirement.name: Normalize all numeric score fields to a consistent scale for LLM interpretabilty

feature.description: Autonomous research agent that discovers provider subspecialties and micro-credentials beyond NUCC taxonomy codes. Combines CMS public data (NPI, Medicare utilization, Part D prescriptions), board certification sources (ABMS), and professional society directories. Produces structured subspecialty data that feeds into provider quality scoring.

story.description: Build a research agent that discovers all surgery subspecialties available in the data. Starting from NUCC surgery taxonomy codes, cross-reference with ABMS board structure, CMS Medicare procedure codes (HCPCS/CPT), and Part D prescriber patterns. Map each subspecialty to its authoritative data source and assess programmatic accessibility (API, scrapable directory, partnership required). Verify results against Delaware provider data.

requirement.requirement: The session token display MUST separate the nonce from the GUID so a human can visually verify each part. The display MUST show: (1) Signed token (the encrypted signature), (2) Nonce (the two timestamps extracted from the token), (3) GUID (the session identifier extracted from the token). The nonce and GUID MUST be displayed as separate labeled fields. The presentation in the right panel (after EvaluateCare or SharedServices handoff) MUST be identical to the presentation in the left panel. Both panels MUST use the same labels, layout, and format.
requirement.name: Display nonce and GUID as separate labeled fields with identical format in both

requirement.requirement: For non-production environments (local, dev, qa), if session-token verification or mutual-authentication handshake (per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-002) fails to complete or does not return a definitive VERIFIED/FAILED result within 30 seconds, the state is illegal. The UI MUST render a 'Fatal Error' splash in the center panel and display Verified: FAILED in the session verification panel. The UI MUST NOT display 'Pending' for longer than 30 seconds. In production, any runtime security-primitive failure MUST cause the hard process exit defined in EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-004.
requirement.name: Render Fatal Error splash if session authentication fails or times out in non‑PR

requirement.requirement: The session-verification panel rendered in the left (specialty search / guiSessionCell) and right panels MUST include two additional rows below the existing fields: (1) `Env: <ENV>` where ENV is the environment label (LOCAL, DEV, QA, or PROD) of the service that issued the token, derived from the active deployment context; (2) `Time: PST <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>` where the value is the token's `created_at` timestamp reformatted to America/Los_Angeles timezone (Pacific Time, observing daylight saving). Both rows MUST appear in both the left and right panel renderings so a human operator can verify which environment served the token and at what time without consulting external tools.
requirement.name: Session token display must include Env and PST Time rows in both panels

requirement.requirement: The session_token.origin field returned by /verify-token (and any equivalent endpoint that returns a session_token object) MUST be set to the name of the RESPONDING service (e.g., "EvaluateCare" for EvaluateCare's /verify-token; "SharedServices" for SharedServices'). This origin field is the SELF-IDENTIFICATION of the service that produced THIS response object — it is distinct from the cryptographic token signer (REQ-017, which always identifies FindCare). One service MUST NOT assert another service's identity in any field rendered to the operator. The wrapper's session-verification panel MUST render this origin value as-is, treating it as the responding service's authoritative claim of its own identity. The display proves that the named component received the nonce and token and produced this verification result.
requirement.name: verify-token response origin field self-identifies the responding service

requirement.requirement: Session token mutual authentication MUST pass for SharedServices. The same token FindCare created MUST be the same one SharedServices received.
requirement.name: Enforce SharedServices mutual auth using FindCare-created session token

requirement.requirement: Any call from FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices to one another MUST complete a mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ handshake. A failed or incomplete handshake is a fatal error per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-008.
requirement.name: Mutual-authentication TLS 1.2+ for FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices inter-

requirement.requirement: The session token MUST use a stable GUID that identifies the session for its lifetime. The nonce (timestamps) MUST be regenerated fresh on every inter-service call. The GUID MUST NOT change between calls within the same session. The nonce MUST NOT be reused across calls. Every ChatHealthy component (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) that receives a token MUST update the last_used timestamp in the nonce to prove it processed the token at that time. Reusing a nonce is a replay attack vector and fails NIST 800-53 SC-23 (Session Authenticity).
requirement.name: Session token uses stable GUID and freshly regenerated nonce on each call

requirement.requirement: On startup every server MUST exercise each security primitive it uses (session-token generation, signature signing and verification, credential redaction, mTLS handshake, key decryption, authentication check). If any exercise fails the process MUST exit with a non-zero code. A server MUST NOT serve any request after a failed startup exercise. Exit codes: 78 (configuration failure — missing library, missing cert, missing env var, malformed primitive output), 77 (permission denied on cert or key file), 70 (unexpected internal error). Stderr MUST name the primitive that failed.
requirement.name: Startup must test security primitives; exit on failure with specific codes

requirement.requirement: EvaluateCare and SharedServices HF Space deploys MUST include findcare.crt (base64-PEM) as an HF Space Secret named FINDCARE_CERT_PEM. On startup, each backend MUST decode this secret and write it to CERTS_DIR so session_token.verify_session_token can validate incoming tokens signed by FindCare. Absence of this secret is a fatal error per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-008.
requirement.name: Deploy findcare.crt as FINDCARE_CERT_PEM secret and decode to CERTS_DIR on start

requirement.requirement: Every session token generated by a ChatHealthy service MUST include an `origin` field whose value is the name of the originating service (FindCare, EvaluateCare, or SharedServices). The token's signature MUST be produced with that service's own private key. Any service receiving a token MUST verify the signature using the named origin's public certificate and MUST reject the token if the origin field does not match the signing key. The session token display — both the left panel at creation and the right panel after a cross-service handoff — MUST render the origin value as a labeled field so a human can visually confirm which service signed the token.
requirement.name: Session token must include and display service origin, signed and verified per-s

requirement.requirement: When the user transfers page ownership to EvaluateCare or SharedServices, the right-panel mutual-authentication request (/verify-token) MUST be issued by the browser directly to the cold-button service (the new owner) and MUST NOT be proxied through FindCare. The browser MUST use the cold service's environment-specific URL (HF Space URL for dev/qa/prod, https://localhost:PORT for local) as the request target. The cold service's /verify-token response — including the verified session token — MUST be the source of the data rendered in the right panel. This ensures the right panel reflects the actual active service's verification, not FindCare's proxied view of it, and is independently verifiable by inspecting the browser DevTools Network tab. CORS on EvaluateCare and SharedServices MUST allow the wrapper origins (localhost, dev.chathealthy.ai, qa.chathealthy.ai, chathealthy.ai). The /session call (token issuance) MUST continue to target FindCare since FindCare is the sole token issuer. Verification: Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py and Code/deploy/devSmokeTestPyTest.py TestStep25.test_push_shared_services MUST register a network listener before the SharedServices banner button click and assert (a) at least one POST to SHARED_URL+'/verify-token' (direct call) and (b) zero POSTs ending in '/shared/verify-token' (no proxy). See BUG-VERIFY-TOKEN-PROXY-001.
requirement.name: Browser must call cold-button service directly for verify-token (no FindCare proxy)

Move prime rule into governance JSON and add two runtime enforcement points
story.description: The prime engineering rule lives only in CLAUDE.md today and has no hook-driven enforcement. This story moves the rule text verbatim into engineering_rules.json and adds two runtime enforcement entries that execute via the existing hook architecture: prompt_verify_directive (UserPromptSubmit) and response_claim_audit (Stop). Both executors live inside the renamed hook manager AnthropicsClaudeCodeHookManager.py.

requirement.requirement: Above all else: Claude MUST NOT make any misrepresentations. Before stating anything, Claude must conduct sufficient research - reading project files, code, requirements, and external sources as needed - so that Claude can only: state a verified fact, state that it does not know, or ask a clarifying question. This rule takes precedence over all other directives when Claude is interacting with the human operator.
requirement.name: Claude must never misrepresent; always verify facts through sufficient research
Materiality threshold for Claude's communication in non-production
requirement.requirement: In all non-production environments, a possible consequence to an action a human user asks Claude Code to do - either as an analysis task or as one that will change state in a reversible way - must not be surfaced to the human operator when that possible analytical or factual potential has less than a 2% probability of occurring.

The prime rule MUST be encoded as a Rule entry in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json with at least two enforcement entries that execute at runtime via the existing hook architecture: (1) prompt_verify_directive fires on UserPromptSubmit and, when the user prompt asks about external-system behavior, injects a hard directive requiring Claude to cite a tool result from this turn or to say 'I don't know - let me verify'; (2) response_claim_audit fires on Stop, scans Claude's just-finished response for definitive claims about external systems, and writes a violation record when no Read/Grep/Bash/WebFetch tool call in the same turn touched that system. Both executors live inside the renamed hook manager (AnthropicsClaudeCodeHookManager.py). The CLAUDE.md preamble is replaced by a one-line pointer to the rule ID.
requirement.name: Prime rule enforced via runtime hooks: verify directive, claim audit, rule id in

feature.name: Brain Consistency
feature.description: Ensures all brain JSON data is internally consistent, cross-referenced, and free of orphaned records. Enforcement mechanisms run deterministically on boot and at check-in.

story.description: On the first user prompt, Claude Code MUST boot the governance singleton and ask the user to select an operating mode (1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot). There MUST be no SessionStart hook. Known bug: BUG-AUTH-001.

requirement.requirement: CLAUDE.md MUST state only that the boot class governs the session.
requirement.name: CLAUDE.md states only that boot class governs the session

requirement.requirement: Each Claude Code session MUST complete a deterministic, non-circumventable boot sequence before any other work. The sequence is: (1) load the governance brain and run compliance checks; (2) at the end of boot, ask the user exactly two questions in order and block all other assistant output until both are answered — Q1: mode selection per REQ-010; Q2: orphan triage per REQ-011. The sequence MUST NOT be skippable, paraphrasable, summarizable, or deferrable by Claude Code. Implementation MAY use any hook topology (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop-hook validator, blocking-reply pattern) so long as the user-observable behavior holds: every new session begins with those two questions presented verbatim, in order, with no other assistant output preceding them.
requirement.name: Enforce deterministic boot: governance + 2 mandatory verbatim questions before I

requirement.requirement: After boot completes, Claude Code MUST ask the user to select an operating mode: 1 = Unattended, 2 = Normal, 3 = Idiot. Claude Code MUST NOT proceed until the user has made a selection.
requirement.name: Prompt user to select mode after boot; block execution until selection is made

requirement.requirement: Orphan triage is the second of the two boot questions. After the user answers REQ-010, Claude Code MUST ask a single yes/no question: 'Triage orphan bugs?' If the user answers no, boot completes and normal work begins. If the user answers yes, Claude Code MUST present the orphan bug table and the user chooses how many to triage this boot — one, several, or all. Triaging an orphan means assigning it a req_id or closing it. There is no per-orphan defer option and no obligation to triage every orphan; the single yes/no gate governs whether the list is shown at all, and within 'yes' the user drives how many get worked.
requirement.name: Boot question: Ask user 'Triage orphan bugs?' and present table if answered yes

requirement.requirement: Every action taken within this project MUST be governed by any applicable rule found in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json. These engineering rules MUST be in Claude's 1,000,000 token context and MUST be checked before any action for compliance. If an order from a human or a task Claude or an agent of Claude contradicts any rules, Claude CANNOT take that action or follow that order.
requirement.name: Enforce compliance with engineering_rules.json before any action is taken

requirement.requirement: The user MUST NOT be forced to login twice during the boot sequence. A single interactive login event per identity provider is the limit; a second consecutive prompt for the same user to the same provider within one boot is a failure. If the first login produced a valid session or cached credential, the boot sequence MUST reuse that credential rather than re-prompt.
requirement.name: Prevent duplicate login prompts per identity provider during one boot sequence

requirement.requirement: The boot class MUST be a single Python file with __main__ and a chathealthy_devops_boot class. main() dispatches to the class by mode (prompt, tool_call, prompt_result, session_end). There is no boot mode — boot is triggered by the prompt handler on first call. Every mode handler MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally. The finally block MUST always call sys.exit() to return control to Cursor/Claude Code. All modes MUST fail open on exception.
requirement.name: Single Python boot class file with strict handler and exit constraints

requirement.requirement: inform_claude() MUST serialize singleton state (version, framework, build, brain file list, constraints, non-allow governance matrix cells) and the orphan table into additionalContext in the hook response. Called from the prompt() path on first boot.
requirement.name: Serialize singleton state and orphan table into additionalContext on first boot

requirement.requirement: chathealthyai_brainboot.json MUST be deleted. brain/machine_artifacts/boot/ directory MUST be deleted. All references to both in chathealthy_devops_boot.py and governance_matrix.json MUST be removed.
requirement.name: Delete chathealthyai_brainboot.json and boot dir, remove all references in code

requirement.requirement: Boot MUST only occur once per session. On SessionEnd, the boot flag in .claude/ChatHealthySettings.json MUST be set to FALSE. On a successful boot from within Anthropic's UserPromptSubmit hook, the flag MUST be set to TRUE. Each subsequent call from the hook MUST check the flag to determine whether the session needs to be booted. If ChatHealthySettings.json or the boot flag cannot be found, an error message MUST be output to the user and no boot is attempted. If SessionEnd does not fire (crash, force-quit), the next session's first prompt will hit the error state and inform the user.
requirement.name: Enforce single boot per session using boot flag in ChatHealthySettings.json

requirement.requirement: SessionEnd hook MUST clear the booted flag in .claude/ChatHealthySettings.json on every invocation. SessionEnd MUST be wrapped in try/except/finally and MUST fail open. SessionEnd is known not to fire on Cursor window-close or auto-compaction; the SessionStart hook (REQ-007) is the primary clearer, and SessionEnd is the secondary clearer for clean exits (/logout, /exit, /clear).
requirement.name: SessionEnd hook clears booted flag in ChatHealthySettings.json, fails open

requirement.requirement: Three context-resident artifacts MUST be loaded into the Claude Code session context at every session start, and MUST be re-injected after any context compaction: (1) brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json — active bug register, loaded in full; (2) brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json — engineering rules, loaded in full; (3) test_output/backlog_stories.json — story-level pruned view of agile_backlog.json covering Epic → Feature → Story only. The story view carries story metadata (story_id, title, description, parent_feature, sprint, size, status, accepted_by, orphan, approval) plus an integer requirement_count per story. It does NOT carry requirement bodies, pytest pointers, realized_by arrays, or any node below story. The full agile_backlog.json (~521K tokens) is NOT context-resident; specific requirement bodies, pytest ids, and realized_by data MUST be fetched from the canonical brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json via Read when Claude needs them. Canonical brain content lives on disk under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ and is never stored anywhere else. The story view is a derived artifact — gitignored, regenerated at session start from the canonical source — it does not replace the source. A pytest MUST verify: (a) @-imports for the three context-resident artifacts are present in the root CLAUDE.md; (b) every current file under Code/DataPipelines/ matching the listed extensions (minus excluded dirs) has a corresponding @-import; (c) every @-imported file exists and is non-empty; (d) no @-imported path is stale. A git pre-commit hook MUST regenerate the DataPipelines @-import block when any file under Code/DataPipelines/ is added, moved, or deleted; if the block is stale, pre-commit MUST fail. Purpose: these artifacts are the ones Claude is most prone to shortcut-reasoning about — grepping instead of reading, guessing instead of checking, proposing duplicates because the original was never loaded. Making the backlog's high-level shape (9 epics / 83 features / 301 stories) context-resident removes the option to grep-and-punt for structure. Requirement bodies remain on-demand because loading the full backlog at ~521K tokens would consume more than half the 1M context window for content that is rarely needed in full. History: agile_backlog.json was attempted in context-residency 2026-04-18 and was replaced with the story-level view the same day. EPIC-008-F-003-S-002-REQ-T-003 (the flat pipe-delimited req_index.txt view) is deprecated in favor of this story-tree view. API source: Claude Code memory docs at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md — '@path/to/import' syntax, 'Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch', 'CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length', 'Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session.' Hook-based injection is NOT a viable substitute because per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks cap additionalContext at 10,000 characters with overflow saved to file + preview — too small for these artifacts.

requirement.requirement: Per-artifact load confirmation. After each session boot, the diagnostic MUST emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012. Each line MUST cite the full project-relative path of the artifact. Silent success is not permitted. The diagnostic signal may come from the InstructionsLoaded hook log, a direct content canary, or both; the reporting format is one line per artifact regardless of source. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts — REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list; any change to scope belongs there, not here.
requirement.name: Emit one confirmation line per context-resident artifact after session boot

requirement.requirement: Load-failure short message. If any context-resident brain artifact fails load verification at session boot (per REQ-012 and REQ-017), the diagnostic MUST output a single short failure line (one line, under 200 characters) that names the failing artifact and classifies the failure as exactly one of four reasons — no more, no less: invalid_json | hash_unreadable | not_loaded | hash_mismatch. A long explanation is a violation of this requirement — follow-up detail belongs in a separate report, not the verdict line.
requirement.name: Short one-line artifact load failure message with exact reason classification

requirement.requirement: Load verification procedure. For each context-resident artifact as defined in REQ-012, the diagnostic MUST execute exactly four steps in order, short-circuiting on the first failure: (1) validate the file as JSON — on failure emit 'invalid_json'; (2) compute sha256 of the file on disk and retain it — on I/O or hash failure emit 'hash_unreadable'; (3) confirm the harness loaded the file into context (InstructionsLoaded event fired for that file_path) — on absence emit 'not_loaded'; (4) recompute sha256 at the InstructionsLoaded event and compare to the hash from step 2 — on inequality emit 'hash_mismatch'. If all four steps pass, emit one 'LOADED' line per REQ-015. These four failure reasons are exhaustive: the diagnostic MUST NOT introduce a fifth category (e.g. timeout, truncation, attention_drift, unknown). Any observed failure that does not map to one of the four reasons is a gap in the procedure, not a new reason. This requirement MUST NOT name specific artifacts — REQ-012 is the single source of truth for the artifact list.
requirement.name: Verify context-resident artifacts using four-step diagnostic with strict error,

requirement.requirement: The Claude Code boot sequence MUST execute 100% from artifacts resident in this project's git repository. No dependency on files outside the repository (user home directory, global Claude Code configuration, machine-level config, external URLs fetched at boot time) is permitted for the boot path. A clean clone of the repository, opened in Claude Code on any machine, MUST boot deterministically to the same governance state as any other. External services (LLM APIs, Cloudflare-hosted schemas, cloud billing dashboards) MAY be contacted after the boot sequence completes, but the boot sequence itself MUST NOT require them.

story.description: Runtime requirements for the brain — specifically WHERE ChatHealthy.AI brain content is persisted on disk and WHERE it must be at runtime (i.e. loaded into Claude's active context). Brain content lives under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Files outside that tree, including Claude Code's and Cursor's harness-managed Markdown files (CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, MEMORY.md and Claude's auto-memory topic files under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/), are NOT brain storage regardless of their content type. At runtime, brain content MUST be accessible to Claude without a disk Read (context-resident, per EPIC-008-F-003-S-001-REQ-T-006). The mechanism is harness-level @-imports from a project-root file (CLAUDE.md) that point at the brain JSONs and derived JSON views of brain JSONs.

requirement.requirement: Before creating any bug record in brain/machine_artifacts/content/bugs.json, Claude MUST search the register for a semantically duplicate or closely-related existing bug and update the existing record rather than create a new one when a match is found. Updates MUST focus on conciseness, accuracy, and fidelity to the evidence. When the bug is novel, Claude MUST insert it under a logical parent requirement (its req_id) in the register. When no logical parent requirement exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the bug with req_id = ORPHAN_BUG, flag it for human's async review at the next boot's orphan triage, and proceed with its work.
requirement.name: Prevent bug duplication; update existing or escalate/flag if no parent exists

requirement.requirement: Before creating any requirement, story, feature, or epic in brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json, Claude MUST search the backlog for a semantically duplicate or closely-related existing entry and update the existing record rather than create a new one when a match is found. Updates MUST focus on conciseness, accuracy, and fidelity to the evidence. When the entry is novel, Claude MUST insert it under a logical parent — requirement under story, story under feature, feature under epic. When no logical parent exists: in Normal or Idiot Mode (v4-004) Claude MUST escalate to human and wait for a decision before inserting; in Unattended Mode Claude MUST insert the entry with orphan = true under the nearest ancestor, flag it for human's async review, and proceed with its work.
requirement.name: Search backlog for duplicates before inserting new agile artifacts

requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy.AI brain content MUST be persisted on disk under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ and nowhere else. Claude Code's and Cursor's harness-managed Markdown files — CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, MEMORY.md and Claude's auto-memory topic files under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ — are NOT brain storage. Those MD files are reserved for harness instructions (CLAUDE.md family) or Claude's ungoverned working memory (MEMORY.md, per v4-037) and MUST NOT carry brain content. @-imports from CLAUDE.md that point at brain JSON files are the required mechanism to make brain content runtime-resident — they do not move the content into the MD file; the content stays on disk in JSON under brain/machine_artifacts/content/. Governing rule: v4-040.
requirement.name: Persist brain content only in brain/machine_artifacts/content/, not in MD files

requirement.requirement: When any of bugs.json, engineering_rules.json, or agile_backlog.json is edited during a session, Claude MUST flush the stale copy from its context and reload the current on-disk version before taking any further action governed by that file. The in-context copy MUST NOT lag the on-disk canonical copy across any action that reads or reasons about the file.
requirement.name: Flush and reload updated JSON files before any governed action

requirement.requirement: The system MUST write a byte-stream copy of brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json to test_output/req_index.txt at every UserPromptSubmit boot and at every session_end. Each write MUST overwrite any prior file at that path. test_output/ MUST be a gitignored project-local folder. CLAUDE.md MUST @-import test_output/req_index.txt. The canonical agile_backlog.json MUST remain the single authoritative source of backlog content. session_end MUST delete the prior test_output/req_index.txt before writing its regenerated copy. The copy format MUST be newline-delimited pipe-separated fields, one requirement per line, columns in order: epic_id, feature_id, story_id, req_id, priority, status, approval, orphan, requirement_text.
requirement.name: Write byte-stream copy of agile_backlog.json to test_output/req_index.txt on key

story.description: Create and maintain deterministic deployment scripts for local, dev, qa, and prod. Each script builds, packages, and deploys all components (FindCare, EvaluateCare, Website) to their respective targets (HuggingFace Spaces, Cloudflare Pages). Scripts MUST be idempotent, testable, and environment-aware.

requirement.requirement: Every deploy script MUST use the following standard port assignments: port 80 (HTTP redirect to HTTPS), port 443 (Website wrapper), port 7860 (FindCare backend + React frontend), port 8001 (EvaluateCare), port 8002 (CHShared). These port numbers MUST be identical across all environments (localhost, dev, qa, prod).
requirement.name: Enforce standard port assignments across all environments in deploy scripts

requirement.requirement: Build, version, and framework identifiers are stored as a single document in the MongoDB Atlas cluster `chathealthyfrontend` (appName `ChatHealthyFrontEnd`), database `{ENV_PREFIX}_System`, collection `version`, document `_id='current'`, with fields: build (integer), version (string), framework (string). All three backend /health endpoints MUST read these three fields from this document. Every git commit that is not part of a deploy pipeline MUST increment the build field by exactly one, enforced by a post-commit hook that writes the new value to MongoDB. A deploy pipeline MUST NOT change any field in this document. The version and framework fields MUST NOT be changed by any automation; they MUST be changed only by a human, and only after human UAT sign-off.
requirement.name: Enforce build, version, and framework document handling and update constraints

requirement.requirement: The Playwright smoke test MUST read the build field from /health on each environment being compared. If the build numbers differ the test MUST fail with a message naming both builds. The test MUST NOT report success when two environments are running different code or configuration. This technical requirement MUST NOT be considered a substitute for EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-002, which requires the build number to be displayed in the environment banner for human verification.
requirement.name: Fail Playwright smoke test if compared environments' /health build fields differ

requirement.requirement: Every HuggingFace Space deploy workflow MUST preserve the target Space's README.md across the push. README.md carries the HF Space frontmatter configuration (sdk, python_version, license) and MUST NOT be wiped. If README.md is missing after a deploy, the deploy is in violation.
requirement.name: Preserve README.md with frontmatter during HuggingFace Space deploy workflow

requirement.requirement:
A Playwright pytest localSmokeTestPyTest.py MUST execute the following 31 steps in order against any environment. Every step MUST pass. The target domain is a parameter: localhost (local), dev.chathealthy.ai (dev), qa.chathealthy.ai (qa), chathealthy.ai (prod).
1. [EPIC-008-F-004-S-003-REQ-B-001] Navigate to http://{domain}. Verify the browser redirects to https://{domain}.
2. [EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-002] Verify the environment banner is visible and contains the correct environment label, Version, Framework, and Build with correct values matching the deployed system.
3. [EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-003] Verify the banner contains a control to test Shared Services. PROD WAIVER: This control MUST NOT appear in production. Skip this step in prod.
4. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-003] Verify the splash page renders with the correct first 25 words of the welcome message.
5. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-004] Verify there is a text input and the cursor is focused so typing goes to the right place.
6. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-005] Type "Find me a bone doctor in Delaware" and submit.
7. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-006] Verify a list of specialties appears in the left panel.
8. [EPIC-006-F-010-S-004-REQ-B-007] Verify the specialty list is contained in a scroll window with a maximum of 12 visible items. The list MUST NOT overflow the left panel.
9. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-005] Verify a list of providers appears in the center panel.
10. [UX-CTRL-003-REQ-006] Verify the bottom panel (Selected for Evaluation) shows zero providers.
11. [UX-CTRL-003-REQ-007] Select up to 3 providers (or all if fewer than 3) by clicking the select control on provider cards.
12. [UX-CTRL-003-REQ-008] Verify the selected providers appear in the bottom panel.
13. [EPIC-006-F-024-S-003-REQ-T-002] Click the Evaluate These Providers button.
14. [TEST-SIM-001-REQ-012] Verify that EvaluateCare has control of the entire frame.
15. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-002] Verify that the calls between FindCare and EvaluateCare are done with mutual authentication using TLS 1.2 or above.
16. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-010] Verify the right panel displays the providers that were moved.
17. [EPIC-005-F-001-S-001-REQ-B-011] Verify the right panel shows the session token proving mutual authentication, the same token FindCare created is the same one EvaluateCare received.
18. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-007] Verify the signed and unsigned token forms are displayed in distinct colors.
19. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-003] Verify the nonce changed from the original FindCare token. The GUID MUST remain the same. The nonce MUST be different, proving EvaluateCare processed a fresh token.
20. [EPIC-006-F-024-S-003-REQ-B-002] Verify the center panel displays EvaluateCare and is still unimplemented.
21. [TEST-SIM-001-REQ-014] Change a value in the specialty filter panel (e.g. uncheck a specialty checkbox).
22. [TEST-SIM-001-REQ-014] Verify control returns to FindCare, the splash page reappears.
23. [TEST-SIM-001-REQ-015] Verify the text input renders and the cursor is focused for typing.
24. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-003] Verify the nonce changed again on return to FindCare. The GUID MUST remain the same. The nonce MUST differ from both the original and the EvaluateCare nonce.
25. [EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-003] Push the Shared Services button in the banner. PROD WAIVER: Skip this step in prod.
26. [EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-004] Verify that the SharedServices server has control of the entire frame. PROD WAIVER: Skip this step in prod.
27. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-002] Verify that the calls between FindCare and SharedServices are done with mutual authentication using TLS 1.2 or above. PROD WAIVER: Skip this step in prod.
28. [EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-005] Verify the center panel displays Shared Services and is still unimplemented. PROD WAIVER: Skip this step in prod.
29. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-001] Verify the same session token mutual authentication test passes for Shared Services. PROD WAIVER: Skip this step in prod.
30. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-003] Verify the nonce changed from the FindCare return nonce. The GUID MUST remain the same. The nonce MUST differ from all previous nonces, proving SharedServices processed a fresh token. PROD WAIVER: Skip this step in prod.
31. [EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-006] Verify all pages are served over HTTPS from the correct servers (443, 7860, 8001, 8002).

Notify Human user with work station generated sound
story.description: A single, OO bell-ringing capability used by every caller in the codebase that needs to notify the human at their workstation — fatal pipeline errors, deploy completion, Claude Code completion events, and future workstation notifications. One class (BellRinger), one location, three ring patterns (once, n-times, until-acknowledged), with optional MongoDB event logging and Pushover cloud alerts.

requirement.name: Class supports ring-once mode
requirement.requirement: BellRinger MUST expose a ring_once method that emits a single beep with configurable frequency and duration.

requirement.name: Class supports ring-n-times mode with configurable interval
requirement.requirement: BellRinger MUST expose a ring_n_times method that emits N beeps with configurable frequency, duration, and interval between beeps.

requirement.name: Class supports ring-until-acknowledged mode
requirement.requirement: BellRinger MUST expose a ring_until_acknowledged method that starts a daemon thread emitting beeps every N seconds until stop() is called. The method MUST be idempotent: a second call while a continuous ring is already in progress is a no-op.

requirement.name: Class invokable from any Python module without subprocess overhead
requirement.requirement: BellRinger MUST use winsound (Windows in-process audio) when available, falling back to a subprocess PowerShell call only if winsound is unavailable. Cloud / headless environments (WEBSITE_SITE_NAME, SPACE_ID) MUST be detected and skipped silently.

requirement.name: Class logs bell events to admin.BellEvents when MongoDB configured
requirement.requirement: When constructed with a MongoDB client, BellRinger MUST insert an event document into admin.BellEvents on every log_event_and_ring invocation. Document fields: ts, event_type, message, context, priority, hostname.

requirement.name: Class emits Pushover cloud alert for high/fatal priorities
requirement.requirement: When PUSHOVER_TOKEN and PUSHOVER_USER environment variables are set, BellRinger MUST emit a Pushover alert for log_event_and_ring calls with priority in (high, fatal). Fatal priority MUST use Pushover priority 2 with retry/expire for guaranteed delivery.

requirement.name: Single class location
requirement.requirement: The single bell-ringing class MUST live at projectRoot/architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/code/bell_ringer.py. No ad-hoc bell-ringing code elsewhere in the codebase.

requirement.name: All callers invoke this class; no ad-hoc bell code elsewhere
requirement.requirement: Every caller in the codebase that rings a bell MUST invoke BellRinger. Inline PowerShell beeps, raw winsound calls, or alternate bell-ringing classes are forbidden.

requirement.name: Fatal pipeline errors invoke ring-until-acknowledged
requirement.requirement: Fatal pipeline errors (QualityGateFailure, unhandled exceptions in the overnight pipeline, parity verification failure) MUST invoke BellRinger.log_event_and_ring with priority='fatal', which triggers ring_until_acknowledged.

requirement.name: Bell continues until human acknowledges
requirement.requirement: A continuous bell (ring_until_acknowledged) MUST keep ringing until stop() is called explicitly by the human or by a downstream condition that signifies acknowledgment.

requirement.name: Claude Code completion events invoke ring-once
requirement.requirement: When a Claude Code background agent or significant task completes, the completion handler MUST invoke BellRinger.ring_once (or the bell_ringer.py CLI with pattern=once) to notify the human at their workstation.

feature.name: Audit — Technical, Business, Regulatory and Corporate Governance
feature.description: This feature encompasses all the audits that must be done to maintain technical and business history, integrity and regulatory and corporate governance.

story.description: A deterministic Python orchestrator dispatches disposable AI workers to analyze git history, brain artifacts, and current code to identify lost capabilities, undocumented changes, and gaps between intent and implementation. The orchestrator is 100% deterministic — all state is on disk, all decisions are file-existence checks. AI is used only inside workers for code analysis. Audits MUST NOT create state changes — they only maintain their own notes and documents, and produce findings and recommendations. The orchestrator loops until all jobs are complete or a human sets the stop command in the control file.

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST examine every version of every file in the git repository to establish a complete lineage of what was built, changed, and removed.
requirement.name: Audit all file versions for complete git repository lineage

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that the brain documents as intended but that does not exist in the current codebase. The brain is the authoritative source of intent.
requirement.name: Identify capabilities intended by brain but missing from current codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every capability that was built and subsequently lost due to uncontrolled changes, code rollbacks, or data loss.
requirement.name: Audit identifies capabilities lost via uncontrolled change, rollback, or data

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST identify every AI call, system prompt, and LLM integration that existed in any previous version and determine whether it is active, intentionally replaced, or lost.
requirement.name: Audit all past AI calls, prompts, LLMs; flag active, replaced, or lost ones

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST cross-reference all findings against the agile backlog, bugs, design documents, business plan, work log, punch lists, unrealized ideas, and all other brain artifacts to determine whether each loss is documented or undocumented.
requirement.name: Audit cross-checks findings against all artifacts for documented or undocumented

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce findings categorized as: undocumented losses, documented but unplanned recoveries, and intentional replacements. Each finding MUST include evidence from git history or brain artifacts.
requirement.name: Categorize audit findings; each must include git or brain evidence

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST produce actionable recommendations for each finding, prioritized by user impact, with effort estimates and a proposed recovery approach.
requirement.name: Audit recommendations prioritized by user impact with effort and recovery plan

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST be repeatable. Running the audit again on the same codebase MUST produce the same findings. The audit is idempotent.
requirement.name: Audit must be repeatable and idempotent, yielding same findings on same codebase

requirement.requirement: The audit output MUST be consumable by both humans (readable report) and machines (structured JSON). The CEO is the primary consumer.
requirement.name: Audit output as human-readable report and structured JSON for CEO consumption

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST NOT modify any source code, database records, brain files, or deployed artifacts. It is a read-only operation. Output is limited to the audit directory only.
requirement.name: Audit is read-only, modifies nothing, output limited to audit directory

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST run to completion autonomously without requiring human intervention beyond the initial start command.
requirement.name: Audit runs autonomously to completion after initial start command

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST survive infrastructure failures (crashes, restarts, context loss) and resume from the last completed unit of work.
requirement.name: Audit recovers from failures and resumes from last completed unit of work

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST track and report its own cost (token consumption) as part of its output.
requirement.name: Audit must track and report its own token consumption in its output

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST have numbered findings where the most important findings are at the top with the lowest number and the least important findings have the highest numbers.
requirement.name: Audit findings numbered by importance, highest priority at top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST make recommendations based on the findings of how to address and remediate each finding.
requirement.name: Audit must recommend remediations for each finding

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST describe its methodology at the top of the report.
requirement.name: Audit report must include methodology description at the top

requirement.requirement: The audit MUST document its assumptions under methodology and above findings.
requirement.name: Audit documents assumptions under methodology and above findings

requirement.requirement: Each audit finding MUST be supported with evidence of at least one example from both the codebase (which may be that no code exists) and from the brain (a known best practice, a brain artifact reference, or code with file and line ranges).
requirement.name: Audit finding must cite code and brain evidence examples

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST be a pure Python script with no AI dependencies. All decisions MUST be based on file existence checks and JSON parsing. No LLM calls in the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Pure Python orchestrator with file checks, JSON parsing, no AI or LLM calls

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST loop continuously until all jobs are complete or a human sets the command to stop in the control file. No other mechanism may stop the orchestrator.
requirement.name: Orchestrator loops until all jobs finish or control file stop command is set

requirement.requirement: All orchestrator state MUST be persisted to disk in a control file (control.json). The orchestrator MUST NOT depend on Claude Code context or conversation memory for any decision.
requirement.name: Persist orchestrator state to control.json; no reliance on memory for decisions

requirement.requirement: Each job MUST write a checkpoint file to disk upon completion. If the orchestrator restarts after a crash, it MUST skip completed jobs by checking for existing checkpoint files.
requirement.name: Write checkpoint files on job completion; skip completed jobs after restart

requirement.requirement: AI workers MUST be spawned as disposable agents with no prior context. Each worker receives a self-contained prompt from a file and writes its output to a checkpoint file. Workers have no knowledge of the orchestrator or other workers.
requirement.name: Spawn disposable AI workers with isolated, self-contained prompts and outputs

requirement.requirement: The orchestrator MUST record token usage and duration from each worker in the control file. Total token spend MUST be visible to the human at all times via the control file.
requirement.name: Record per-worker token usage/duration; show total spend in control file

requirement.requirement: All worker output MUST use structured JSON with predefined schemas. No free-form text output. Every finding MUST include evidence (commit hash, file path, or brain file reference).
requirement.name: Worker output uses structured JSON schemas with evidence for every finding

requirement.requirement: The audit output MUST be expressed as a JSON document having a strict schema. The output MUST be in strict compliance with that schema.
requirement.name: Audit output as JSON document with strict schema compliance

story.name: Codebase History Audit — Deterministic Agent

story.description: Two-pass scanner: Pass 1 streams every source file, builds a map of all definitions (classes, methods, functions) and all references (calls, imports, attribute access). Pass 2 reconciles — anything defined but never referenced is dead and must be deleted. Two modes: check-in (staged files only, fast) and full regression (entire codebase).

requirement.requirement: Pass 1 must stream source files without holding full source in memory. It accumulates a definitions map (name, file, line) and a references set (names used). Memory proportional to symbol count, not source size. DR-008 compliant.
requirement.name: Stream pass 1 source, accumulate symbol maps, memory ~symbol count, DR-008

requirement.requirement: Pass 2 walks the definitions map and checks each against the references set. Any definition with zero references and no framework-invocation decorator (FastAPI route, Azure trigger, governance hook) is reported as dead code.
requirement.name: Report unreferenced definitions without framework decorators as dead code in Pas

requirement.requirement: Check-in mode scans only staged files (git diff --cached). If a staged file adds a function, verify something calls it. If it deletes a function, verify nothing else calls it. Must complete in under 5 seconds for typical commits.
requirement.name: Check-in scans staged files for function usage and finishes under 5 seconds

requirement.requirement: Dead code found during check-in mode blocks the commit. Dead code found during full regression is reported but does not block (informational for promotion review).
requirement.name: Block commits for dead code in check-in; report only in full regression

story.name: Dead code scanner — two-pass symbol analysis

feature.description: The Brain as a deployed component. Agentic infrastructure for running the company — assignments, governance, audit, grooming, monitoring. MongoDB-backed, API accessible.

feature.description: Implementation of the brain infrastructure — the system of record for governance, requirements, rules, design decisions, and all machine-readable artifacts that govern the system.

requirement.requirement: ALL utterances MUST be durably captured and archived to MongoDB. MongoDB is the permanent record. Zero utterance loss is the target. The system MUST NOT silently drop events.
requirement.name: Durably capture and archive all utterances to MongoDB without loss

requirement.requirement: Sensitive keys (API keys, connection strings, passwords, credentials) MUST NEVER be written to MongoDB. These values MUST be redacted with [Sensitive content redacted]. Profanity MUST be redacted with [expletive redacted].

requirement.requirement: Utterances older than 24 hours MUST be removed from local storage after they have been archived to MongoDB.

requirement.requirement: Every action on the log MUST be recorded with who, what, and when.

requirement.requirement: The conversation log service MUST start automatically on system boot without operator intervention.
requirement.name: Conversation log service auto-starts on system boot without intervention

requirement.requirement: If MongoDB is unavailable, utterances MUST be retained durably and archived when MongoDB becomes available. No utterance may be lost due to a downstream outage.

requirement.requirement: If the service fails, the human operator MUST be informed as soon as they appear after an absence, or immediately if they are present. The notification MUST include what failed and why.
requirement.name: Notify operator on return or immediately of service failure with details

requirement.requirement: The human user MUST be able to restart the service at any time. The service MUST be fully operational within 10 seconds of restart.
requirement.name: Service restarts available anytime; full operation within 10 seconds

requirement.requirement: The Claude Code hook MUST capture each utterance and POST the raw payload to a localhost HTTP sidecar. The hook MUST complete in under 100ms. The hook MUST NOT parse, redact, transform, or write to any file. If the sidecar is unreachable, the hook MUST append to a local emergency fallback log and return.
requirement.name: POST utterance to localhost sidecar; fallback log if unreachable; complete <100

requirement.requirement: A persistent Python/FastAPI sidecar (PID 1) MUST maintain a warm Apache Kafka producer connection. It MUST accept HTTP POST requests from the hook, enqueue the raw payload to Kafka, and return HTTP 202 immediately. It MUST NOT do any processing beyond enqueue.
requirement.name: Sidecar maintains warm Kafka producer, enqueues POST payloads, returns 202

requirement.requirement: A persistent Python consumer (PID 2) MUST read from the Kafka topic, perform GPT-4.1-mini redaction (B004), assign a unique key (CH_KEY_ followed by a generated GUID), add timestamps (B002), and archive to MongoDB. It MUST use manual commit only after successful MongoDB write. If it crashes mid-processing, Kafka MUST redeliver the message (at-least-once delivery).
requirement.name: Python consumer with GPT-4.1 redaction, unique key, timestamp, MongoDB, manual-0

requirement.requirement: Apache Kafka MUST run in a Docker container on the local machine. The Kafka broker MUST use KRaft mode (no ZooKeeper). The topic MUST retain messages for 24 hours. A single partition is sufficient.
requirement.name: Kafka in Docker using KRaft, 24hr retention, single partition, no ZooKeeper

requirement.requirement: The C# Windows service (ChatHealthyClaudeLogMgmt) MUST be a supervisor only. It MUST start the Docker Kafka container if not running, start the sidecar (PID 1), start the consumer (PID 2), monitor both, and restart them if they die. requirement.name: C# Windows service supervises Kafka, sidecar, consumer, restarts, no business

requirement.requirement: The C# Windows service MUST be configured for AUTO_START so it runs on system boot without operator intervention.

story.description: Scan brain JSON files for schema compliance and structural integrity.

requirement.requirement: The JSON scanner must validate all brain JSON fields that are constrained by a controlled vocabulary (constrained_by in schema.json). For each constrained field, the scanner must read the allowed values from the referenced CV in controlled_vocabularies.json and reject the file if any record contains a value not in the CV. The scanner must run as a pre-commit gate and block check-in of any brain JSON that fails CV validation. This applies to all CV-constrained fields including but not limited to bugs.json resolution_status (CV-009) and type (CV-008).
requirement.name: Validate all controlled vocabulary fields in brain JSON as pre-commit gate
Pre-commit is the single gate; any file failure blocks the entire commit
requirement.requirement: Pre-commit is the SINGLE rule-enforcement gate. The pre-commit scanner MUST run every engineering rule with an executor (the rules in engineering_rules.json) plus schema validation and any other rule check, scoped to the files being staged. If ANY single staged file fails ANY single rule, the entire commit MUST be blocked (return non-zero exit code). Commits are atomic: every staged file passes every applicable rule and the commit proceeds, OR the whole commit is blocked. Pre-push runs ONLY the network operation; it does NOT re-enforce rules (pre-commit already did). This eliminates the 'commit passed but push fails' trap.

The scanner validates v4-032: every plural-named field in every brain JSON must be an array. Every array member must conform to the singular-named schema. The scanner reads the schema to discover plural/singular pairs and validates the data against them. Implementation may be AI scan or code scan.
requirement.name: Scan JSON for plural field arrays and validate members via singular schema
Single 'name' label across the agile_backlog hierarchy
requirement.requirement: Every level of agile_backlog.json - epic, feature, story, requirement - MUST use a single 'name' field as its human-readable label. Schema and existing data MUST conform; no 'title' field anywhere in the hierarchy. A one-time data conversion MUST execute: any missing 'name' is mined from the record's existing description/requirement text. For any node where the existing content is inadequate to derive a meaningful name, the converter MUST emit a warning naming the specific node, AND the file MUST FAIL validation - no silent fallback.

requirement.name: Engineering rule MUST trace to an approved requirement
